text:
Jordan (sales): Heads-up: Nimbus Health hit a 413 during their POC upload. Demo aborted. They said app sent a single JSON bundle.
Ivy (solutions): Which upload flow? presigned parts or direct POST?
Jordan (sales): Direct POST from their legacy exporter. Reported size ~18MB, but they used UTF-16LE so it inflates.
Ravi (eng): 413 usually at the edge. Can you paste the gateway log line?
Jordan (sales): ``[WARN] 2026-04-02T09:11:12Z upstream returned 413: Request Entity Too Large``
Lina (devex): If it's presigned we recommend chunked part uploads. For direct POST we can either bump client_max_body_size for the demo or ask them to switch encoding/compression.
Ivy (solutions): We should avoid env changes if possible. Can we ship a one-line patch to their exporter to switch to UTF-8 and gzip? That usually fixes token bloat.
Jordan (sales): They prefer not to change exporter mid-demo. Any quick server-side options?
Ravi (eng): Temporary bump is easiest. I can set demo route to 40M. But note: even if the body is accepted, tokenization could still exceed model limits.
Lina (devex): Good point. What model are they calling in the demo?
Jordan (sales): `open-compat-3b` (demo config).
Ravi (eng): That profile has a 32k token request limit. If post-decode token count >32k, the model will truncate. We need client-side truncation or a preflight check that warns users before send.
Ivy (solutions): Can we implement a lightweight preflight: send metadata (size + encoding) and return a suggested remediation (gzip, UTF-8, chunk) before upload? Makes demo friendlier.
Lina (devex): We already have a tiny preflight snippet in the docs. I'll paste it: 
```
// pseudo
let meta = {size, encoding}
let ok = await post('/poc/preflight', meta)
if (!ok.can_upload) showWarning(ok.suggestion)
```
Also show estimated token count using tiktoken-lite.
Jordan (sales): I'll ask Nimbus to try switching to UTF-8 and enabling gzip; if they refuse, Ravi please bump the demo host route and add an alert in Grafana for body-size spikes.
infra-bot: config-change: nginx/demo-route.client_max_body_size=40M requested by Ravi -> pending approval
Ravi (eng): Approved and deploying to staging now.
infra-bot: deploy: nginx/demo-route update -> success 00:00:17
Jordan (sales): Retried with Nimbus 3: upload now returns 200 but output truncated. They say first few paragraphs missing.
Lina (devex): That's truncation at the model side. Confirm the assembled prompt token count.
Jordan (sales): After decoding UTF-16LE contents into UTF-8 (they left encoding wrong initially) it's ~38k tokens.
Ravi (eng): Bingo. Exceeds 32k limit. Options: smart trim oldest tokens (fastest), split into multiple context-aware calls (harder), or move to a long-context profile. For POC, smart trim + UI warning.
Ivy (solutions): Also call out cost implications if they increase model context. 38k tokens x multi-request = expensive; include that in the proposal.
Lina (devex): I can add a demo client change: estimate tokens, if > max show "Content too big: trimming oldest sections" and include a "download full transcript" link. Use our client-side token-slice util.
Jordan (sales): I'll coordinate with Nimbus: offer two options in follow-up email: (1) quick fix: UTF-8 + gzip + chunking, (2) short-term server bump + demo truncation + guidance.
Ravi (eng): Filed ENG-POC-413-NIMBUS to track (epic). I'll also add a checkbox to enable per-customer higher body limit if they commit to Dedicated capacity.
infra-bot: ticket-created: ENG-POC-413-NIMBUS (#12841)
Ivy (solutions): Great. Lina, can you add the preflight snippet to the sales POC runbook and attach the token-estimate example?
Lina (devex): On it. Will include code sample and an example UI message.
Jordan (sales): Nimbus implemented UTF-8+gzip and retried 3: full context present, demo passed. Customer asked about pricing for larger contexts.
Ivy (solutions): Sent pricing note: longer contexts increase token bill; recommend Dedicated for predictable throughput and cost controls.
Ravi (eng): Closing temporary nginx increase tonight. Also leaving runbook steps and the per-customer route automation TODO.
Jordan (sales): Thanks all 389 closing thread.
